messages:
devon: heads-up — finished A/B run for v2q-lite on prod-slice A. short summary below.

nina: ping the numbers?

devon: intent_accuracy delta +0.4% (±0.6). cost_per_token -22%. p95 latency +18ms. concerning: hallucination_rate on long-docs (>4k tokens) jumped +1.7% absolute (2.8x relative).

ash: which cohort? cold starts?

devon: cohort name: longdoc-heavy-rerank. ~3.6k samples. problem crops up when KV merge hits quantized compression path for sequences >4096 — quality drifts.

jia: what gating config did you use for the canary?

devon: pasted the canary config we used:
```json
{
  "canary": {
    "initial_fraction": 0.01,
    "max_fraction": 0.25,
    "promotion_step": 2,
    "slo": {"latency_p95_ms": 220, "error_rate_pct": 0.5},
    "quality_gates": {
      "fidelity_score_delta": -0.8,
      "hallucination_rate_delta_pct": 1.0,
      "variance_multiplier": 2.0
    },
    "auto_fallback": {
      "enabled": true,
      "trigger_window_minutes": 30,
      "consecutive_windows": 2
    }
  }
}
```

nina: that hallucination gate is 1.0% delta — we saw +1.7% absolute so fallback should have fired. did auto_fallback trigger?

devon: it didn't. root cause: telemetry pipeline tags those longdocs as "cold-kv-warmup" and routes them through low-priority sampling that lacks realtime hallucination eval. auto_fallback consumes only realtime metrics, so it never saw the spike.

ash: oof. we can't promote canaries when real-time quality hooks are disabled for a cohort.

jia: quick mitigation: exclude cohorts without realtime_quality from progressive promotions. config snippet suggestion:
```yaml
canary.exclude_cohorts:
  - name: longdoc-heavy-rerank
    realtime_quality: false
```

devon: implemented the exclude rule in staging; pushing config change now. deploy-bot: apply change to canary-staging-12 but do not alter traffic weights.

deploy-bot: ack — applying config to canary-staging-12 in dry-run then patch. will hold weights. :gear:

nina: long-term, should hallucination gates be absolute or relative percent uplift? baseline for that cohort is tiny so relative looks huge.

ash: recommend hybrid: require absolute_delta > 0.5% AND relative_uplift > 30% of baseline. avoids noisy small-cohort trips. also add monotonic hysteresis for promote (require 2 consecutive healthy windows).

jia: agreed. also add a lightweight sentinel metric for hallucination on longdocs (heuristic token-based signal) so auto_fallback can act even when full offline eval isn't available.

devon: design note: calling this "cohort-holdfast" — when triggered, the cohort is held from promotion and marked. promotion resumes only after 2 consecutive windows meeting both absolute+relative thresholds. also tag incident: cohort-holdfast/longdoc.

nina: what's the rollout timeline?

devon: telemetry PR: https://git.internal/r/telemetry/1234 — staging tests green. will request ops +1 before prod rollout.

ash: +1 from me. ops, please confirm revert playbook covers immediate model-pin to v2-stable and traffic shift under 60s.

jia: ops sign-off: verify rollback path pins model and routes cohort slices to stable. fallback must annotate offending model with tag `cohort-holdfast/longdoc`.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary-config rollout window 02:15 UTC. will run dry-run then apply. will report success/fail.

devon: follow-up: adding onboarding checklist item — "no progressive promotion for cohorts without realtime_quality hooks". open item for docs and runbook updates. :memo:
